keyECGEvidence: Morphology: Narrow QRS, no clear P waves, abrupt onset
Pre-Event Note: Abrupt onset after exertion/caffeine; hemodynamically stable
modelResponse.primaryEtiology: Sympathetic overdrive secondary to stimulant ingestion (Caffeine)
modelResponse.mechanism: Excessive adrenergic stimulation leading to premature atrial or junctional firing.
contributingFactors: Recent ingestion of caffeine ('Two cups of coffee')
Hemodynamic stability allowing for observation/pharmacological intervention

rejectedAlternatives.why: TSH is within normal limits (2.2 mIU/L), and the acute onset is strongly linked to caffeine intake.
Potassium (4.0 mmol/L) and Magnesium (2.0 mg/dL) are both within normal reference ranges.

recommendedActions: HOLD any scheduled medications if they are adrenergic agonists. If the patient is symptomatic, consider IV benzodiazepine (e.g., Lorazepam) for vagal maneuver.
If stable, monitor rhythm closely. Advise patient to cease caffeine intake.
If symptoms persist or worsen, proceed with cardioversion if necessary, maintaining Full Code status.
uncertainty: The exact origin of the SVT (SA node, AV node, or atrial tachycardia) cannot be definitively determined without rhythm strip morphology beyond the provided summary fields.
